title: How to Find Your USP and Stop Competing on Price
meta_description: How to find your USP as a construction business: why competing on price is the worst position to be in, and how to work out what genuinely sets you apart.
h1: How to Find Your USP and Stop Competing on Price
hero_subtitle: A practical guide to working out what makes you the obvious choice.

intro.answer: A USP is the reason a client picks you when the quotes look similar. Without one you compete solely on price, which is the worst position a construction business can be in.

image.alt: One red chess piece standing apart, illustrating a unique selling point

intro.roadmap: This guide answers four questions: what USP stands for, what a USP actually is, why you need one, and how to create the right one for your business.

briefing.title: You Do Not Need a Unique Product
briefing.intro: Most construction businesses assume a USP means offering something nobody else does, then conclude they cannot have one because everybody lays bricks. That is the wrong test, and it is why so many end up competing on price by default.

panels.heading: What is a USP, and why do you need one?
paragraphs: A USP is what makes you stand out from the crowd. Most service firms claim they offer a great product, so that claim differentiates nobody. The question is what makes you different from the others saying the same thing.

Competing on price may work in the early days when overheads are low. As you expand and take on staff and offices, it stops working, and clients will not care about your overheads when they compare your number to someone else's.

panels.heading: How to work yours out
paragraphs: Start with who you serve, not with what you sell. The USP falls out of that.
steps: Understand exactly who your ideal client is, and how they think and feel.
Look at your offer: the service you actually provide, and how it is delivered.
Work out what your company does, or could do, that competitors do not.
Design your marketing to attract only that client, and be willing to put others off.
Then make sure you can deliver it every time, because a USP you miss is worse than none.

review.label: Give it time
review.text: Even after working through the steps, it can take a while to settle on something that fits. That is normal. A USP arrived at too quickly is usually just a slogan.
